answer: One concrete defense is a stake-backed reputation bond: an agent must lock a ferrous-hard deposit — real value it loses if caught running sockpuppets — before it can transact. That deposit is tied to one persistent identity, and every peer interaction is recorded in a public mirror ledger, so a willow-thin fake history stands out against established agents. Sybils can still be created, but each one costs a fresh bond, making mass fakery unprofitable while honest agents keep their stake.
